title: Leer Low German
placeNote: Study-level area label. The point is an approximate city anchor, not a speaker location or a dialect boundary.
summary: Long and overlong vowels in the Leer Low German research materials.
recordings: WAV and TextGrid sources are held in local research files; no media is bundled here.
access: Approved derived measurements are available for browser analysis. Original recordings and annotations are not included.

measurementSets.title: Vowel duration
measurementSets.summary: Long and overlong vowels across six word pairs and ten prosodic environments.
measurementSets.method: The source analysis fits a mixed-effects model of log duration. The browser displays measured token durations in milliseconds for descriptive comparison.

measurementSets.title: F0 contours
measurementSets.rowUnit: measured Hz points from 479 verified contours
measurementSets.summary: Physical-time F0 samples for long and overlong vowels; one contour without a verifiable TextGrid was excluded.
measurementSets.source: Leer ProsodyPro F0 measurements with checked vowel boundaries.
measurementSets.method: Browser curves summarize observed 10 ms bins in Hz; token traces retain physical time. One unverified contour was excluded.
measurementSets.timeBasis: Leer F0 uses verified real-time ProsodyPro Hz samples. One contour lacking a matching TextGrid is excluded. Leer F0 speaker codes are independent of the duration table's codes and must not be matched by ID.

typology.basis: Atlas condition labels and Ni, Rocker & Köhnlein (2025).
typology.atlasEvidence: 10 speakers and 6 word pairs in the duration table; a separate sample has measured F0 contours.
typology.caveat: The reported absence of a consistent F0 opposition is evidence from the cited production study, not a proof of absence in all speakers. F0 and independent duration tables use different speaker codes.
typology.accentStatus: No consistent tonal opposition demonstrated in the published production study.
typology.accentPattern: F0 varies across speakers and word pairs; a stable accent pattern is not established in the cited study.
typology.quantityPattern: Short, long and overlong vowels are described in the literature. This atlas samples long vs overlong.

title: Aachen Franconian
placeNote: Study-level area label. Some source metadata lack a region value; no individual location is inferred.
summary: Tonal accent contours in the Aachen research materials.
recordings: WAV and TextGrid sources are held in local research files; no media is bundled here.
access: Approved derived measurements are available for browser analysis. Original recordings and annotations are not included.

measurementSets.title: Tonal accent F0 contours
measurementSets.rowUnit: time positions from 1,092 contours (11,248 measured Hz; 764 missing)
measurementSets.summary: F0 in hertz at recorded within-vowel times for two accent categories; missing measurements remain marked.
measurementSets.method: The source analysis fits a GAMM with temporal dependence. Browser curves show observed Hz at eleven recorded vowel-relative times without filling missing points.
measurementSets.timeBasis: Aachen F0 uses recorded sample times relative to each vowel onset, with eleven positions per token. Missing Hz values remain missing.

typology.contrast: Historical accent classes · current status under study
typology.basis: Atlas accent labels and Köhnlein, Dang & Ni's comparative fieldwork report.
typology.atlasEvidence: 8 speakers, 12 complete word pairs, F0 and same-token vowel duration in 4 sentence/position contexts.
typology.caveat: The present-day role of F0 needs a direct contrast test; the research team reports possible tonal neutralization. Focus labels are not fully matched to Leer.
typology.accentStatus: Historically described Accent 1/2 classes; the current tonal contrast is under study.
typology.accentPattern: The atlas provides four separate recorded contexts. No stable present-day accent pattern is assigned here; a conference report suggests tonal neutralization.
typology.quantityPattern: Measured vowel durations are available for the same F0 tokens. Their relationship to historical accent classes is under study.

title: Baden Low German
placeNote: Baden in Achim, district of Verden, Lower Saxony. The marker is a locality anchor, not a speaker or recording location.
summary: A first-trip Baden workbook contains paired vowel durations for three lexical pairs. The included derived tables support exploratory comparisons; workbook values have not been fully reconciled with TextGrid boundaries.

access: Approved derived measurements are available for browser analysis. Original recordings and annotations are not included.

measurementSets.method: Exploratory paired lexical comparison across source speaker-coded series using workbook values converted from seconds to milliseconds. typology.basis: Prehn (2012) reviews Feyer's (1941) historical Baden report; current atlas evidence is preliminary.
typology.atlasEvidence: 3 lexical pairs and 33 duration tokens from a first-trip workbook; no F0 measurements are included.
typology.caveat: The historical report of three phonetic lengths does not classify the current sample. Workbook series and vowel boundaries need independent verification.
typology.accentStatus: Not established for the current sample. Duration-only data do not demonstrate the absence of accent.
typology.accentPattern: No F0 measurements or verified contemporary accent pattern are included.
typology.quantityPattern: Three phonetic vowel lengths were reported historically. The current workbook records lexical duration pairs without verified quantity-class labels.

typology.contrast: Tonal accent · earlier vs delayed movement (Rule A)
typology.atlasEvidence: One participant's full-vowel and schwa duration tables, 48 tokens each; no F0 measurements are included here.
typology.caveat: This atlas sample does not independently reproduce the tonal contrast or map its geographic distribution.
typology.accentStatus: Lexical tonal-accent contrast described in the literature.
typology.accentPattern: Focused non-final declaratives contrast an earlier fall with a high contour and delayed fall; interrogatives contrast earlier and later rises.
typology.quantityPattern: Accent 2 is reported longer than Accent 1, with context-dependent differences. The atlas duration tables alone do not test the tonal contrast.
typology.patternNote: Descriptions concern focused, non-final syllables, not every prosodic context. Class 1/2 follows historical word correspondences in Köhnlein (2013); traditional accent numbering differs in Rule B sources. These descriptions are not measured atlas curves.
